questions.q: What does it mean that Cosmos DB's API for MongoDB is 'wire-protocol compatible'?
options: It implements the same binary protocol MongoDB client drivers use, so existing drivers and tools can connect by changing only the connection string
It converts MongoDB queries into Cosmos DB SQL syntax before running them
It is a completely separate product unrelated to Cosmos DB
It only works with a specially rewritten MongoDB driver
questions.explain: Wire-protocol compatibility means the existing driver, unmodified, can talk to Cosmos DB — the real distinguishing feature described in the lesson.

questions.q: What has to change for an existing MongoDB application to point at Cosmos DB's API for MongoDB?
options: The connection string — the driver and query code stay the same
The entire data access layer must be rewritten
The application must be rewritten in a different programming language
Nothing changes; it happens automatically with zero configuration
questions.explain: The lesson's example shows the same driver connecting with only the connection string swapped to point at the Cosmos DB Mongo endpoint.

questions.q: What does the API for Apache Cassandra provide, analogous to the API for MongoDB?
options: Wire-protocol compatibility with CQL, letting existing Cassandra drivers and cqlsh connect to Cosmos DB
A tool that converts Cassandra data into a graph format
Support only for Cassandra's administrative commands, not queries
A completely different query language than CQL
questions.explain: The API for Cassandra implements the CQL wire protocol the same way the API for MongoDB implements the MongoDB wire protocol.

questions.q: What honest caveat does this lesson emphasize about these compatibility APIs?
options: Wire-protocol compatibility does not guarantee 100% feature parity — some operators or commands may be unsupported or behave differently
These APIs are fully identical to native MongoDB and Cassandra in every respect
These APIs are deprecated and should never be used
There is no compatibility documentation available at all
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: real migration work requires checking the feature-support matrix, not assuming full parity.

questions.q: What real-world scenario are the MongoDB and Cassandra APIs best suited for, per this lesson?
options: Lift-and-shift migration of an existing app onto Cosmos DB's global distribution and elastic throughput without a full rewrite
Building a brand-new graph database application from scratch
Replacing the need for the Core (SQL) API entirely in all cases
Running purely relational, foreign-key-enforced workloads
questions.explain: These APIs exist specifically for teams that want Cosmos DB's platform benefits without abandoning their existing MongoDB or Cassandra codebase.
